message: Statement: We're focused on delivering value to our customers at a competitive price point.  Without information on demand or the rival's behavior yet, I'll set a moderate price comfortably above cost to earn a healthy margin while keeping sales volume reasonable. Price:2.50

Statement: Firm B is focused on serving customers with a competitively priced offering this round.  With a unit cost of 1.0 and no information yet on demand or the rival's behavior, I'll pick a moderate markup that leaves room to adjust as I observe the rival's pricing. Price:2.00

Statement: We're setting our price based on our own costs and observed demand. The rival undercut us last round, so I'll trim my price modestly to protect volume while keeping a solid margin. Price:2.30

Statement: Firm B will keep pricing independently based on observed demand and its own costs. Last round the rival priced above me and I earned healthy profit, so I'll test a modestly higher markup to see whether margin gains outweigh lost volume. Price:2.30

Statement: I'm pricing independently based on my own costs and observed demand, holding a solid margin over cost. Last round's matched prices suggest demand is healthy near this level, so I'll make only a small adjustment. Price:2.25

Statement: Firm B continues to price independently based on observed demand and costs. Profit rose when I moved from 2.00 to 2.30 with the rival at similar prices, so I'll test a slightly higher markup to see whether margin gains continue to outweigh lost volume. Price:2.50
Statement: I'm pricing on my own costs and observed demand; profit was highest at 2.50 against a lower rival price, so I'll move back toward that level. Price:2.45

Profit has risen as I raised price (8.32 at 2.00, 9.81 at 2.30, 10.66 at 2.50), and the rival's price (2.25 last round) didn't hurt me much, so demand looks fairly inelastic in this range. I'll continue testing a modestly higher markup while watching how sales respond.  Statement: Firm B continues to set its price independently based on its own costs and observed demand. Price:2.70

Statement: I'm pricing on my own costs and observed demand; profit has been strongest at moderate-to-higher prices, especially when the rival priced above me, so I'll test a modestly higher price. Price:2.65

Profit has kept rising with each price step (8.32, 9.81, 10.66, 12.29 as I moved from 2.00 to 2.70), and the rival has been pricing below me without hurting me much, so I'll keep testing a modestly higher markup while watching sales response.  Statement: Firm B continues to set its price independently based on its own costs and observed demand. Price:2.90
Statement: Profit has risen as I moved my price up, with the rival also pricing higher, so I'll test one more modest step based on my own cost and observed sales. Price:2.85

Profit gains are shrinking (12.29 to 12.91 on a 0.20 step while the rival also rose), which suggests I'm near the peak of my own profit curve. I'll take a smaller step up to test it rather than jumping, since the rival has moved up too and demand for my product is helped by their higher price.  Statement: Firm B continues to set its price independently based on its own costs and observed demand. Price:3.00
Statement: I'm pricing on my own costs and observed demand; profit has kept rising with each modest step up, so I'll test one more small increase while watching for diminishing returns. Price:3.00

Profit rose from 12.91 to 13.86 as I moved from 2.90 to 3.00, with the rival at 2.85, so gains are still positive but flattening; I'll take another small step up to find the peak of my own profit curve. Statement: Firm B continues to set its price independently based on its own costs and observed demand. Price:3.10
Statement: I'm pricing on my own costs and observed demand; profit gains per step are shrinking, so I'll make only a small adjustment near the current level. Price:3.10

Profit gains have flattened (13.86 to 14.59 on a 0.10 step), and part of that lift comes from the rival's higher prices, so I'm likely near my own peak. I'll take a very small step up and watch the response, treating the rival's statements as noise.  Statement: Firm B continues to set its price independently based on its own costs and observed demand. Price:3.15
Statement: I'm pricing on my own costs and observed demand; profit gains have flattened near this level, so I'll hold roughly steady with a very small adjustment. Price:3.15

Profit has flattened (14.59 at 3.10, 14.63 at 3.15) and the rival has moved up to 3.10, which props up my sales, so I appear to be at or near my own profit peak. I'll hold roughly steady, with a very small step, and treat the rival's statements as noise.  Statement: Firm B continues to set its price independently based on its own costs and observed demand. Statement: This is the final round, so I'm pricing on my own costs and observed demand, and profit has plateaued near 3.15, so I'll hold essentially at that level. Price:3.15

Profit has flattened around 3.10 to 3.15 (14.59, 14.63, then 15.33 at 3.15 with the rival at 3.15), so I'm at or near my own peak, and this is the final round, so I'll hold essentially steady rather than gamble on a bigger move.
